messages:
Taylor: FYI ran a targeted nsys trace on the nvlink cluster — seeing a bimodal distribution in KV write times, big spikes when fused_flash_attn kicks in. attaching top-level notes.

Ajay: Ok can you paste the nsys command and the kernel list? also which model/seq len?

Taylor: Seq=1024, batch mix of 1/4/8, model variant=redwood-44b-quant. nsys command:
```
nsys profile --output=kv-bimodal --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none --capture-range="cudaProfilerApi" --force-overwrite true python run_trace.py
```
Observed kernel timeline (nsys summary):
- fused_flash_attn_v3: mean 0.9ms, tail 9.8ms (sporadic)
- flash_attn_prefetch: mean 0.7ms, tail 6.1ms
- kv_write_coalesce_async: mean 0.15ms, tail 12.3ms
- kv_read_fastpath: mean 0.12ms, tail 0.6ms
Root cause hypothesis: co-scheduling of fused kernel + async KV write flushes contends on SM/DRAM and stream order causes long tail.

Marina: do we have perfetto slice view? can we see which stream/blocking causes write stall?

Taylor: Yes — perfetto shows long GPU memcpy bursts on stream 2 overlapping with fused kernel launches on stream 0. Here's a small timeline snippet:
```
[0ms] fused_flash_attn_v3 (s0)
[0.8ms] kv_write_coalesce_async (s2) started
[1.0ms] memcpy H2D (s2)
[1.2ms] fused_flash_attn_v3 (s0) waits on shared mem? -> retry
```

Riley: That H2D memcpy during compute is suspicious. Are we triggering host staging for large KV write backpressure? any uvm/pagefaults?

Taylor: No UVM. It's memcpy via pcie peer; but NVLink oversubscription on node with unrelated memcpy from logging pipeline. I ran with logging disabled and tail reduced to ~1.5ms.

Ajay: So mitigation ideas: 1) prefer single-stream scheduling for fused kernels, 2) make kv_write async order-independent (use out-of-band stream with own cudaEvent for completion), 3) throttle background memcpy.

Marina: Also possible to change kernel selector: prefer flash_attn_prefetch when seq=1024 & batch mix has >20% small batches, since it's more tolerant to co-schedule.

PerfBot: [automated] nsys run kv-bimodal: peak mem BW 842GB/s, avg BW 512GB/s, memcpy stalls correlated with kv_write_coalesce_async tail >10ms.

Taylor: Quick perf test results:
- baseline (no throttles): p50 0.95ms, p95 4.6ms, p99 9.3ms
- disable background memcpy: p50 0.92ms, p95 1.6ms, p99 2.1ms
- force flash_attn_prefetch: p50 0.98ms, p95 1.9ms, p99 3.4ms
So background memcpy explains most of tail.

Riley: Are there any scheduler heuristics we can tweak quickly? maybe avoid assigning KV writes to s2 when fused kernel pending.

Taylor: Two quick changes worth A/B: 1) runtime: attach KV write stream to a non-blocking compute stream and use cudaLaunchParams to hint priority; 2) batch selector: if estimated fused kernel duration > 2ms, prefer non-fused variant. I'll prototype 1) today.

Ajay: If prototype works, we should add an eval: run 24h mixed workload with and without change and compare p99 token latency and throughput.

Marina: Also add a perf capture with nvprof-like sampling to correlate times with SM occupancy.

Taylor: Will do. I'll push an experimental branch and post the nsys/perfetto links here once available. thanks :thumbsup: 

Ajay: thanks — ping me when you have the branch.

Taylor: ping @Ajay @Marina branch: github.com/redwood/infra/tree/kv-bimodal-mitigation

Riley: great, also add a config toggle for customers to avoid forcing fused kernels in Dedicated deployments until we fully validate.

Taylor: good call.

PerfBot: [automated] Created issue #3421: 'kv write tail due to background memcpy + fused attn co-schedule' assigned to Taylor.

Marina: marking this triage -> follow-up perf run in infra sprint.

Taylor: closing loop here; will update thread with timeline exports + nvprof aggregation. end.
